title: [finding] shadcn: sheet/sidebar carry load-bearing local edits that are documented in prose but NOT declared patches — a `--force` sync drops them, and one of them does it silently
body:
Fell out of #4996 (PR pending), which vendored byte-verbatim registry fixtures for all four patched families and asserted the declared anchors against them. Out of scope there: that card owns anchor *verification*, not the question of which edits are declared in the first place.

## Fact

With the vendored fixtures in place, `applyLocalPatches(name, upstreamBytes)` reproduces the shipped primitive **byte for byte** for `dialog` and `slider`, and **does not** for `sheet` and `sidebar`. The residue is local edits that live only as prose in `packages/components/shadcn-components.json` (`localEdits`), with nothing in `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs` re-applying them:

| file | undeclared local edit | what a `--force` sync does |
|---|---|---|
| `sheet.tsx` | `hideOverlay` prop suppressing `<SheetOverlay />` | drops it → call sites fail to type-check (**loud**) |
| `sidebar.tsx` | Tailwind v4 `[--var]` → `(--var)` migration (925051db6) | drops it → **compiles, renders, emits invalid CSS browsers discard** (**silent**) |
| `sidebar.tsx` | `eslint-disable react-hooks/purity` on the skeleton | drops it → Lint fails (**loud**) |
| `sidebar.tsx` | unconditional `data-collapsible` + `group-data-[state=collapsed]:` qualifiers | drops it → styling/test-locator behaviour changes, no gate |

`shadcn-components.json` already says the quiet part out loud for `sheet`: the i18n patch is declared and re-applied automatically, *"so unlike the `hideOverlay` edit above it does not depend on anyone remembering it."*

## Why it matters

This is the exact hazard `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs` opens with — `--force` bypasses the `localOnlyLines` refusal by design and takes the edit with it, and a type-check cannot see the loss. The module's answer is "declare the edit". Two of these four are caught downstream by other gates; **the Tailwind v4 one is not caught by anything**, and it is explicitly documented as load-bearing (the v3 spelling compiles to a bare custom-property name on Tailwind 4.x — invalid CSS).

## Not asserting a severity

Nothing is broken today: no `--force` sync has run, and #4996's fixtures now pin the *declared* anchors. This is about which edits are declared, which is a judgement call about cost (declaring the Tailwind migration as a patch family means anchoring ~20 class strings) versus the silence of the failure mode. Options worth weighing include declaring only the load-bearing subset, or an offline assertion that the shipped file contains no v3 `[--var]` spellings at all — the latter is much cheaper and catches the same regression from the other side.

Filed unassigned, `finding` only, no `pm:queue` — observation class, for PM triage.
